Hi Theresa — great to meet you and the MedBridge team earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so our security/solutions folks can produce a short evidence pack you can take to legal/compliance.

Call recap (one-liner): MedBridge wants an interactive assistant to help therapists prepare care plans; primary concerns are PII redaction in prompt input, whether model outputs are retained, and what logs/telemetry are stored and for how long.

Can you confirm the following from your side?
- Example prompt shapes (we requested a small, redacted sample during the call) — attaching ours for context.
- Required maximum retention for any prompt text or output (e.g., 30 days, 90 days, never).
- Whether you need token-level logs for debugging or only aggregate/latency metrics.
- Whether you require customer-managed encryption for persisted artifacts (SSE-KMS) or if Redwood-managed keys are acceptable.

Next steps from Redwood: Monica will outline storage options and default telemetry retention; Ben will surface SOC 2 / compliance artifacts where available. We can prepare a short doc mapping: prompt -> where stored -> TTL -> encryption in transit/at rest.

Attachments: post-call-sample-prompts.json (redacted examples)

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the recap and fast turnaround. A few clarifications from MedBridge: 

- Example prompts: attached a redacted therapist->assistant exchange in this thread (we removed names and MRNs).
- Retention ask: ideally 30 days for full prompt+response for product telemetry, but any PII must be masked immediately; we can accept 0 days for raw PII if you support masking at ingestion.
- Logs: we only need aggregate latency/error telemetry for GA; token-level logging is only acceptable in a secured, customer-managed store for debug sessions (on request).
- Encryption: we prefer customer-managed KMS for anything persisted beyond 7 days.

Please let us know whether Redwood has a mode to mask PII at ingestion (redact before storage), and whether you provide an option to disable storage entirely for a given project or route.

Also, can you confirm turnaround for a short architecture note and a SOC2 redaction? We need docs to present to our legal by next Tue.

Best,
Theresa
Director of Product, MedBridge Health

Hi Theresa — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; attaching a short options sheet and a sample masking config for your security team.

Summary of Redwood behavior (defaults and configurable options):
- Default (hosted API):
  * Prompt input: stored for 30 days by default for telemetry and quality monitoring.
  * Model outputs: stored for 30 days by default (used for evals/quality).
  * Token-level telemetry: NOT stored by default; we collect aggregated metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) with PII filtered out.
  * KV cache: ephemeral in-memory only during the request/streaming session; it is not persisted to disk in hosted mode.

- Configurable options for enterprise customers / private deployments: 
  * No-persist mode: you can opt into a mode where neither prompts nor outputs are written to persistent storage. This is available for Dedicated and Private deployments or as a policy on hosted routes for Enterprise customers.
  * Server-side masking (ingestion masking): Redwood can run a lightweight regex/ML-based masker at the API edge to redact common PII (names, MRNs, SSNs, emails) before any persistence. We can supply the masking config (attached) and allow tuning or an allow-list for safe fields.
  * Customer-managed persistence: for Private/Dedicated, persisted artifacts can be routed to customer S3/GCS with SSE-KMS and a retention TTL you control. Redwood provides lifecycle hooks and an API to purge exports on request.
  * Debug sessions: token-level captures can be enabled only for a named debug window and routed to customer-managed storage; otherwise they are never retained.

Operational guarantees and SLAs for retention/exports: 
- Standard turnaround for an audit export (redacted) is 48 business hours.
- We support ad-hoc purges for a workspace/project within 72 hours via the support portal and programmatic API.
- All persisted data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. For customer-managed keys we support AWS KMS & GCP KMS.

Other notes about PII handling:
- We do not persist raw host-level KV caches used for inference.
- For embeddings or reranking features, you can choose to persist embeddings; by default embeddings are ephemeral unless explicitly enabled.
- We keep an immutable audit trail for access/logging metadata (who accessed which route) for 90 days by default; that metadata excludes prompt/output contents unless retention is enabled.

Attachments: redwood-storage-options.pdf, masking-config.yaml

Next steps:
1) I'll prepare a one-page mapping doc (prompt -> storage class -> TTL -> encryption) and a short MOP (mutual action plan) with timeline.
2) Ben will attach SOC2 redacted artifacts and certificate links.

Happy to run a quick 20-min follow-up with your security lead to walk through the masking config.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
